title: HAAD / DOH Abu Dhabi
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public DOH Abu Dhabi health-professional examination syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A 62-year-old man presents with central chest pain radiating to the left arm, diaphoresis, and nausea for the past 40 minutes. His ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads V2 to V4. Which action should be taken first?
options: Administer sublingual nitroglycerin and reassess the pain
Activate the primary percutaneous coronary intervention pathway without delay
Give a loading dose of oral aspirin and clopidogrel and arrange a chest X-ray
Start an intravenous fluid bolus and obtain serial troponin levels over several hours
items.explanation: ST-elevation myocardial infarction requires immediate reperfusion, and in centres with primary PCI capability the affected artery should be opened as fast as possible. Nitroglycerin, oral antiplatelets, and fluids are supportive measures that must not delay the reperfusion call.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 34 weeks of gestation presents with a blood pressure of 162/104 mmHg, a severe headache, and visual disturbances. Her urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is markedly elevated. Which medication should be given first to prevent seizures?
options: Oral labetalol tablets
Intravenous magnesium sulfate
Sublingual nifedipine capsules
Intravenous furosemide
items.explanation: This is severe pre-eclampsia with neurologic features, and intravenous magnesium sulfate is the first-line agent for seizure prophylaxis. Antihypertensives such as labetalol or nifedipine control blood pressure but do not prevent eclamptic convulsions, and furosemide is not indicated.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman is admitted with a painful, red, swollen right calf three weeks after knee replacement surgery. She is tachycardic and slightly hypotensive. Which investigation is the most appropriate initial step?
options: D-dimer assay only, withholding imaging if negative
CT pulmonary angiography performed immediately
Compression duplex ultrasound of the right leg
Ventilation-perfusion lung scanning
items.explanation: The presentation is highly suspicious for deep vein thrombosis, and compression duplex ultrasound is the recommended first-line imaging because it is non-invasive, readily available, and accurate for calf and proximal vein thrombi. D-dimer alone cannot confirm the diagnosis and CT angiography is reserved for suspected pulmonary embolism.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 70-year-old man with a known peptic ulcer presents with sudden, severe epigastric pain, a rigid abdomen, and free air under the diaphragm on an upright chest radiograph. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Start a proton pump inhibitor infusion and oral antacids, then reassess in 24 hours
Arrange upper gastrointestinal endoscopy within the next working day
Begin oral amoxicillin and clarithromycin for suspected Helicobacter pylori eradication
Provide urgent surgical repair with intravenous fluids, antibiotics, and nasogastric decompression
items.explanation: Free subdiaphragmatic air with peritoneal signs indicates a perforated peptic ulcer, a surgical emergency. Definitive management is urgent operative repair supported by resuscitation, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and decompression; conservative or elective measures delay treatment of a life-threatening leak.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 6-year-old child is brought in with a barking cough, stridor at rest, and hoarse voice following a viral upper respiratory infection. There is no drooling or difficulty swallowing. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
options: Nebulized epinephrine and a systemic corticosteroid
Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and observation at home
Endotracheal intubation in the operating theatre
Oral prednisolone only, with no other intervention
items.explanation: The findings are typical of viral croup, and moderate to severe croup with stridor at rest is treated with nebulized adrenaline for rapid airway relief plus dexamethasone or equivalent steroid to reduce recurrence. Antibiotics do not treat a viral illness, intubation is reserved for impending obstruction, and steroid alone works too slowly for the acute stridor.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 45-year-old man with type 2 diabetes presents with polyuria, polydipsia, weakness, and a fruity breath odour. His blood glucose is 28 mmol/L, arterial pH is 7.18, and serum ketones are elevated. Which intravenous fluid regimen is most appropriate initially?
options: 5% dextrose solution at maintenance rate
0.45% sodium chloride at a rate appropriate for severe volume depletion with close monitoring
Hartmann's solution without any insulin therapy
Oral rehydration solution given in place of intravenous fluids
items.explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis requires aggressive intravenous rehydration, typically with 0.9% sodium chloride initially and careful transition to a hypotonic solution once glucose falls, alongside fixed-rate insulin and potassium replacement. Dextrose alone, oral fluids, or fluids without insulin will not correct the ketotic state.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A nurse assesses a conscious 58-year-old man who has just experienced a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that lasted 90 seconds. He is now confused but breathing adequately with a patent airway. What should the nurse do first?
options: Insert an oral airway and begin bag-mask ventilation
Give an intravenous benzodiazepine immediately to prevent another seizure
Place him in the recovery position, protect him from injury, and monitor vital signs
Obtain a computed tomography scan of the brain before any other action
items.explanation: After a self-terminating seizure with a stable airway and adequate breathing, the priority is safety and positioning with continuous observation in the recovery position. Airway adjuncts and ventilation are unnecessary, abortive anticonvulsants are given only for ongoing or recurrent seizures, and imaging is not an emergency nursing action here.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, and dry skin. Her thyroid-stimulating hormone is elevated and free thyroxine is low. What is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Radioactive iodine ablation therapy
Short course of oral prednisolone
No treatment because subclinical disease needs no therapy
Lifelong levothyroxine replacement with periodic dose monitoring
items.explanation: The biochemical picture is overt primary hypothyroidism, which is treated with lifelong levothyroxine replacement titrated against thyroid function tests. Radioactive iodine and steroids are not treatments for hypothyroidism, and untreated overt disease causes significant morbidity.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman in a long-term care facility develops a temperature of 38.9 degrees Celsius, new-onset confusion, and dysuria. Her blood pressure is 88/56 mmHg and heart rate is 118 beats per minute. Which treatment should be started most urgently?
options: Immediate intravenous fluid resuscitation and prompt intravenous antibiotics
Oral trimethoprim for seven days after urine culture
Oral fluconazole and observation for 24 hours
Antipyretics alone until cultures return
items.explanation: An older adult with suspected urinary sepsis showing hypotension and tachycardia needs sepsis-bundle care: rapid intravenous crystalloid and broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics within the first hour, with cultures taken before antibiotics when possible without causing delay. Oral therapy and watchful waiting are unsafe in septic shock.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman visits the clinic with a three-day history of painful vesicles and ulcers on her genitals, dysuria, and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely causative organism?
options: Treponema pallidum
Herpes simplex virus type 2
Haemophilus ducreyi
Neisseria gonorrhoeae
items.explanation: Recurrent or first-episode genital ulcers with vesicles, dysuria, and painful regional lymphadenopathy are characteristic of genital herpes caused by herpes simplex virus. Syphilis typically presents with a painless chancre, chancroid with a single painful ulcer, and gonorrhoea primarily with discharge rather than ulceration.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient with chronic kidney disease stage 4 has a serum potassium of 6.8 mmol/L with peaked T waves on ECG. Which intervention should be implemented immediately?
options: Oral sodium polystyrene sulfonate and repeat bloods in four hours
Emergency hemodialysis as the only acceptable next step
Intravenous calcium gluconate to stabilize the myocardium, followed by measures to lower potassium
Subcutaneous insulin without glucose monitoring
items.explanation: Hyperkalaemia with ECG changes is a cardiac emergency. Intravenous calcium stabilizes the myocardial membrane within minutes, after which insulin-dextrose, beta-agonist nebulizers, and potassium binders shift or remove potassium, with dialysis used when refractory. Delaying membrane protection while arranging dialysis risks fatal arrhythmia.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 50-year-old man reports episodic epigastric pain that wakes him at night and improves with eating. An upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows a duodenal ulcer. Which organism should be tested for and treated if present?
options: Clostridioides difficile
Salmonella typhi
Campylobacter jejuni
Helicobacter pylori
items.explanation: Duodenal ulcers are overwhelmingly associated with Helicobacter pylori infection or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use, so testing and eradication therapy is a core part of management. The other organisms cause enteric infections and are not established causes of duodenal ulceration.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A primigravida at 32 weeks reports decreased fetal movement for the past 12 hours. Examination shows a singleton pregnancy with a normal heart rate. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Arrange urgent obstetric assessment including a cardiotocograph and, if indicated, ultrasound
Reassure her that reduced movement at this gestation is always normal
Perform an immediate caesarean section without further assessment
Advise her to wait one week and return if symptoms persist
items.explanation: Reduced fetal movements always warrant timely assessment, typically with cardiotocography and fetal ultrasound when indicated, because they can be an early sign of placental compromise or growth restriction. Reassurance without assessment, watchful waiting, or immediate delivery without investigation are all inappropriate.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with right-sided pleuritic chest pain, haemoptysis, tachycardia, and a right leg that is swollen and tender compared with the left. Which single investigation most reliably confirms the diagnosis?
options: Chest radiograph
Computed tomography pulmonary angiography
Arterial blood gas analysis
Complete blood count and C-reactive protein
items.explanation: The combination of pulmonary symptoms and unilateral leg swelling suggests pulmonary embolism with deep vein thrombosis, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography is the diagnostic imaging of choice in haemodynamically stable adults. Chest radiography and blood gases support assessment but do not confirm the diagnosis.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A nurse is caring for a patient with community-acquired pneumonia who has an oxygen saturation of 88% on room air, is conscious, and is able to swallow. What is the most appropriate initial oxygen therapy?
options: High-flow oxygen via non-rebreather mask targeting normal saturation rapidly
No supplemental oxygen because the patient is not in respiratory failure
Controlled oxygen therapy via nasal cannulae or simple mask targeting 88 to 92%
Immediate non-invasive ventilation without a trial of oxygen
items.explanation: In acute respiratory failure with hypoxaemia, controlled oxygen therapy titrated to a target saturation of 88 to 92% prevents both worsening hypoxia and, in patients at risk of hypercapnia, carbon dioxide retention. Uncontrolled high-flow oxygen offers no additional benefit and can be harmful, while withholding oxygen or jumping to non-invasive ventilation is inappropriate here.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - General Medicine and Nursing

items.stem: A patient on warfarin for atrial fibrillation is prescribed clarithromycin for a chest infection. The pharmacist notices a high risk of interaction. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Double the warfarin dose for the duration of antibiotic therapy
Continue both drugs unchanged with no monitoring
Stop warfarin completely until the infection resolves
Select an alternative antibiotic with less interaction potential where clinically appropriate
items.explanation: Clarithromycin potently inhibits warfarin metabolism and can dangerously raise the international normalised ratio with bleeding risk. The safest approach is to choose a less interacting antibiotic when options exist, or if macrolide therapy is essential, to increase monitoring and adjust warfarin deliberately rather than empirically doubling or stopping anticoagulation.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A 6-month-old infant weighing 8 kg is prescribed paracetamol at a dose of 15 mg/kg. The available syrup contains 120 mg in every 5 mL. What single dose volume should be given?
options: 5 mL
6 mL
7.5 mL
items.explanation: The required dose is 8 kg times 15 mg/kg, which equals 120 mg. With syrup concentration 120 mg per 5 mL, the volume needed is 5 mL. Under- or miscalculated dosing in infants is a common medication error, so the arithmetic must be verified before administration.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A woman of childbearing age asks for a medication for severe acne. She uses barrier contraception inconsistently. Which acne treatment is contraindicated because of teratogenic risk?
options: Topical benzoyl peroxide
Oral isotretinoin
Topical erythromycin
Oral doxycycline
items.explanation: Isotretinoin is a potent teratogen causing severe fetal malformations, so pregnancy prevention, testing, and contraception requirements are mandatory. Topical retinoids, though less well absorbed, also carry risk; antibiotics and benzoyl peroxide are not teratogenic in this way, though tetracyclines are avoided later in pregnancy for other reasons.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A 70-year-old man taking an ACE inhibitor and furosemide develops acute kidney injury after becoming dehydrated. Which medication should be temporarily withheld?
options: Neither drug should ever be withheld in heart failure
Only the furosemide should be withheld permanently
The ACE inhibitor and furosemide should both be reviewed with temporary withholding of the ACE inhibitor
Aspirin should be withheld instead of the cardiovascular agents
items.explanation: The combination of ACE inhibition and diuretic-induced volume depletion precipitates acute kidney injury by reducing glomerular filtration pressure. The ACE inhibitor is the classic drug to withhold during intercurrent illness or dehydration while ensuring euvolemia, with other concurrent medicines also reviewed by the prescriber.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A nurse is about to administer intravenous gentamicin to a patient with a creatinine clearance of 25 mL/min. What is the most important pharmacokinetic consideration?
options: Gentamicin requires no adjustment because it is metabolized by the liver
The standard dose should be doubled to overcome poor absorption
Gentamicin levels are unnecessary for any patient receiving the drug
Gentamicin is renally cleared so extended intervals or dose adjustment with drug level monitoring are required
items.explanation: Gentamicin is almost entirely eliminated by glomerular filtration, so reduced renal function causes accumulation and ototoxic and nephrotoxic risk. Dosing must be adjusted using extended intervals or nomograms with trough and peak levels and regular creatinine monitoring.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient with severe asthma is prescribed a beta-blocker for angina after a myocardial infarction. Which beta-blocker property would be least appropriate, and why?
options: A cardioselective beta-1 blocker, because non-selective agents markedly increase bronchospasm risk
Any beta-blocker, because all are equally unsafe in asthma
A beta-blocker with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity, because these stimulate bronchi
Propranolol, because it is short-acting and therefore safer
items.explanation: Non-selective beta-blockers block beta-2 receptors in bronchial smooth muscle and can precipitate severe bronchospasm in asthma, so cardioselective agents are preferred when a beta-blocker is truly indicated. Not all agents are equally risky, and intrinsic activity or short half-life does not remove the airway risk.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient taking a monoamine oxidase inhibitor asks about dietary restrictions. Which food item must be avoided because it can trigger a hypertensive crisis?
options: Fresh white rice
Aged cheese and other tyramine-rich fermented foods
Boiled chicken breast
Steamed carrots
items.explanation: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors prevent tyramine breakdown, and tyramine-rich foods such as aged cheeses, cured meats, marmite, and fermented products can provoke a sudden hypertensive crisis. Fresh, cooked, and non-fermented foods carry essentially no tyramine load.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A 55-year-old man on metformin is admitted for a contrast-enhanced CT scan because of suspected pulmonary embolism. Which action regarding his metformin is most appropriate?
options: Continue metformin throughout and after contrast administration
Switch permanently to insulin before the scan
Withhold metformin around the contrast exposure and restart once renal function is confirmed stable
Halve the metformin dose for the rest of his life
items.explanation: Iodinated contrast can precipitate acute kidney injury, and metformin accumulation in that setting raises the risk of lactic acidosis, so it is withheld from before the scan until renal function is reassessed and found satisfactory. Continuing it blindly, or making permanent therapy changes, is not warranted.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A nurse prepares an intravenous insulin infusion for a patient in diabetic ketoacidosis. Which practice best prevents a wrong-dose error with this high-alert medication?
options: Guessing the pump rate from memory because the chart is busy
Drawing up the insulin with the same syringe used for other drugs to save time
Relying on the most junior staff member to prepare the infusion alone
Using a standardized insulin infusion protocol, independent double-checks, and clearly labelled syringes
items.explanation: Insulin is a high-alert medication, and safety is best achieved through standardized written protocols, clear labelling, and independent double-checks by two qualified staff before administration and at every handover. Memory-based dosing, shared syringes, and unsupervised preparation are classic sources of fatal errors.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman with epilepsy becomes pregnant and is taking valproate for generalized seizures. What is the most appropriate counselling point?
options: Valproate carries a high risk of teratogenicity and neurodevelopmental harm, so an urgent specialist review of alternatives is needed
Valproate is completely safe in all trimesters of pregnancy
The dose should be doubled immediately to prevent seizures
All antiepileptic drugs should be stopped the moment pregnancy is confirmed
items.explanation: Valproate has the highest teratogenic risk of the common antiepileptics, including neural tube defects and impaired child neurodevelopment, so pregnancy planning with a neurologist to find the safest effective alternative or minimize the dose is essential. Stopping therapy abruptly risks status epilepticus, which is also dangerous for mother and fetus.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient on a stable dose of clozapine develops a temperature of 39 degrees Celsius, flu-like symptoms, and a markedly elevated C-reactive protein. Neutropenia is confirmed on full blood count. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Continue clozapine and give paracetamol for the fever
Stop clozapine immediately and manage as suspected clozapine-induced agranulocytosis
Double the clozapine dose to stimulate marrow recovery
Add a broad-spectrum antibiotic without altering clozapine
items.explanation: Clozapine can cause agranulocytosis, typically in the first months of treatment, presenting with flu-like symptoms and confirmed neutropenia. The drug must be stopped urgently and haematology input obtained; continuing or up-dosing clozapine risks fatal sepsis.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A nurse realizes just after the shift that she recorded giving a dose of enoxaparin that she did not actually administer. What is the correct immediate reporting action?
options: Delete the entry quietly and administer the dose as soon as the patient asks for pain relief
Amend the record with a false timestamp to hide the delay
Report the error openly through the incident reporting system and ensure the patient receives the dose safely
Ask a colleague to sign that they saw the dose given
items.explanation: Medication administration errors must be disclosed and documented through the organisation's incident system so the patient can be assessed and treated, and so systems can learn. Falsifying records or concealing the omission breaches professional duty, patient safety, and legal obligations.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A patient with a history of anaphylaxis to penicillin is prescribed piperacillin-tazobactam for hospital-acquired pneumonia. What is the most appropriate step before administration?
options: Administer the drug immediately because penicillin allergy does not apply to other beta-lactams
Give a double dose of an antihistamine and proceed with the infusion
Apply a tourniquet above the injection site during the infusion
Escalate to the prescriber and allergy specialist for assessment and selection of a safe alternative or a controlled graded challenge
items.explanation: Piperacillin-tazobactam is a penicillin-class beta-lactam, so a true penicillin allergy is a significant concern. The safest response is to flag it to the prescriber, clarify the nature and severity of the reaction, and choose an alternative antibiotic or use an evaluated delabelling pathway, not to simply pre-medicate and proceed.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A man is prescribed sildenafil and also takes a long-acting nitrate for chronic angina. He asks why the pharmacist refused to dispense them together. What is the correct explanation?
options: The combination causes profound, potentially life-threatening hypotension through exaggerated nitric oxide pathway effects
Sildenafil reduces the absorption of all oral nitrates from the gut
Sildenafil converts nitrates into a toxic metabolite in the liver
The two drugs compete for the same renal tubular secretion causing crystal formation
items.explanation: Sildenafil is a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor that potentiates the cyclic guanosine monophosphate vasodilator effects of nitrates, producing severe and sometimes fatal hypotension. Because of this pharmacodynamic interaction, nitrates are contraindicated and washout periods must be observed before sildenafil is used.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: A nurse is assigned a shift with a heavy workload and realizes that two different patients have been given drugs from look-alike vials with confusingly similar labelling. What is the single best preventive strategy?
options: Keeping both products side by side for staff convenience
Removing high-alert look-alike products from stock, using tall-man lettering, and storing them separately
Relying on colour recognition alone for identification
Abbreviating drug names on labels to save printing space
items.explanation: Look-alike and sound-alike medication errors are mitigated by separating storage, using tall-man lettering for confusing names, removing unnecessary look-alike stock, and employing barcode verification. Colour-only identification and abbreviation of names are themselves error-promoting practices.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Pharmacology and Medication Safety

items.stem: During a central venous catheter insertion, a colleague's sterile field is contaminated when the ultrasound probe cover tears. What should the practitioner do first?
options: Continue the procedure quickly to minimize catheter dwell time
Apply alcohol hand rub to the outside of the drape and continue
Abandon the contaminated setup, replace the sterile equipment, and re-scrub before restarting
Ask another staff member to finish without changing gloves
items.explanation: Once the sterile field is compromised, the only safe action is to stop, discard contaminated items, re-establish asepsis with fresh drapes and instruments, and repeat hand hygiene before proceeding. Rushing on or dabbing the field with alcohol does not restore sterility and exposes the patient to bloodstream infection.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A newly admitted patient has an allergy to latex documented in the chart but is about to be transferred to the operating theatre. What is the most important safety action?
options: Note the allergy in the chart only and assume theatre staff will remember
Give prophylactic steroids and proceed with standard gloves
Remove the allergy documentation to reduce alarm fatigue
Ensure a latex-safe environment is arranged, communicate the allergy to the theatre team, and use latex-free equipment
items.explanation: Latex allergy can cause severe anaphylaxis on exposure, so the allergy must be actively communicated at every handover, the patient's record and wristband flagged, and a latex-free environment with non-latex gloves and equipment prepared. Passive charting and pre-medication do not prevent exposure.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is being prepared for surgery and the surgical site on the abdomen has been marked. Later, the theatre list changes and a different patient with a similar name is wheeled in. What is the most effective safeguard against wrong-site surgery?
options: A formal pre-operative verification and time-out involving the whole team confirming identity, procedure, and site against the marking
Relying on the surgeon's memory of the list
Checking only the wristband while the patient is asleep
Asking the most junior team member to read the consent form alone
items.explanation: The World Health Organization surgical safety checklist, including sign-in and time-out with active verification of patient identity, procedure, site, and consent by the entire team, is the core defence against wrong-site and wrong-patient surgery. Memory checks, single-person checks, and checks after anaesthesia are unreliable.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A nurse accidentally dislodges a peripheral intravenous cannula in an anticoagulated patient, and bleeding soaks the dressing. What is the correct immediate response?
options: Apply ice and leave the patient to call for help later
Apply firm continuous pressure to the site, reassess the patient, and escalate if bleeding does not control
Elevate the limb only without any direct pressure
Reinsert a new cannula at the same site immediately to stop the bleeding
items.explanation: The first response to significant bleeding from a dislodged cannula is direct, firm pressure with the limb elevated as appropriate, followed by patient observation and escalation to senior staff if haemostasis is not achieved or the patient becomes symptomatic. Ice, delay, or immediate re-puncture at the same site do not control bleeding.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A healthcare worker is preparing to enter the room of a patient with suspected multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii requiring contact precautions. Which personal protective equipment is required?
options: A surgical mask only
A particulate respirator and goggles for all contacts
Gloves and a gown, with hand hygiene before and after the interaction
No protective equipment if the worker washes hands afterwards
items.explanation: Contact precautions for multidrug-resistant organisms require gloves and a gown on entry and removal on exit with hand hygiene at both points. Respirators are reserved for airborne precautions such as tuberculosis, and surgical masks alone do not protect against contact spread.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is unconscious and unaccompanied in the emergency department with a life-threatening condition requiring immediate surgery. What is the correct consent pathway?
options: Wait indefinitely until a family member arrives to sign the consent form
Ask a receptionist to sign as a witness to the procedure
Obtain verbal consent from the patient over the telephone after sedating him
Operate under implied consent and the doctrine of necessity to preserve life, documenting the decision thoroughly
items.explanation: Where a competent patient cannot consent and delay would cost life or limb, clinicians act under necessity for the patient's best interests, documenting the rationale. Waiting for relatives, surrogate signing by unqualified staff, or sedated verbal consent are improper or impossible pathways.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: An operating room nurse notices that a surgical instrument tray is missing a countable sponge after wound closure has begun. What should happen?
options: Suspend closure, search for the item, and obtain radiological confirmation before final layers are completed
Close the wound and document the discrepancy in the nursing notes only
Assume the sponge was discarded and continue closure to save time
Ask the scrub nurse to add an extra sponge to the count at the end of the procedure
items.explanation: A retained foreign body is a never event. When counts do not reconcile, the team must stop closure, conduct a systematic search, and obtain an X-ray before the final layers are closed, with clear documentation and incident reporting. Closing on assumption risks a retained item and serious harm.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A staff member reports a needlestick injury from a used hollow-bore needle while assisting with a procedure on a patient of unknown HIV and hepatitis status. What is the correct immediate action?
options: Apply bleach to the wound and continue the shift
Wash the site with soap and water, do not squeeze the wound, and present immediately for occupational health assessment and baseline testing
Take a course of antibiotics prophylactically without seeking assessment
Ignore it because the risk of transmission is negligible
items.explanation: After a percutaneous exposure, the wound should be encouraged to bleed while being washed with soap and water, the event reported at once, and post-exposure prophylaxis and baseline blood tests considered urgently per occupational health protocol. Strong irritants such as bleach damage tissue, and delaying assessment forfeits the window for prophylaxis.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is receiving a packed red blood cell transfusion and develops fever, rigors, and flank pain 30 minutes into the infusion. What is the first nursing action?
options: Slow the transfusion and give paracetamol while continuing observation
Increase the transfusion rate to complete the unit quickly
Stop the transfusion, keep the line open with normal saline, and assess and report the reaction
Change the blood set and restart transfusion at the same rate
items.explanation: Fever, rigors, and flank pain during transfusion suggest an acute haemolytic or febrile reaction, so the infusion must be stopped immediately, venous access maintained with saline, blood samples sent for investigation, and the medical team notified. Slowing or speeding the transfusion prolongs exposure to potentially incompatible blood.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A ward uses an infusion pump whose alarm keeps sounding intermittently. The device is from a batch previously flagged for reliability concerns. What is the best risk-management step?
options: Tape the alarm speaker shut so staff are not disturbed
Switch the pump to gravity infusion without documentation
Ask a student to stand and watch the pump all night
Remove the device from service, tag it, and report the fault through the equipment incident process
items.explanation: A malfunctioning infusion pump, especially one from a flagged batch, must be taken out of service, labelled clearly, and reported so biomedical engineering and the safety team can act. Silencing alarms or ad hoc workarounds defeat engineered safeguards and can kill patients.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A patient with a known history of falls is being prepared for discharge home to a second-floor flat with steep stairs. What is the most appropriate pre-discharge intervention?
options: Arrange a multidisciplinary falls risk assessment including home safety review and modification of risk factors
Provide no assessment because falls are only a hospital concern
Advise the family to buy a walking stick from a pharmacy without assessment
Recommend permanent admission to a care home
items.explanation: Falls risk should be addressed holistically before discharge, combining medication review, gait and balance assessment, vision checks, and an occupational therapy home hazard evaluation with tailored interventions. Generic equipment advice or extreme options without assessment leave the patient at ongoing risk.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is admitted with a pressure injury over the sacrum that was not present on admission. Which classification of incident does this represent, and what should happen?
options: An adverse event that needs no documentation because pressure injuries are expected
A healthcare-associated harm event that must be assessed, documented, reported, and managed under the facility's pressure injury prevention bundle
A manufacturing defect incident about the hospital mattress only
A patient non-compliance issue requiring reprimand
items.explanation: A pressure injury developing after admission is a preventable healthcare-associated harm event. It requires accurate staging, prompt wound care, root-cause investigation, incident reporting, and reinforcement of repositioning, nutrition, and skin assessment bundles rather than being dismissed as inevitable.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A patient is undergoing magnetic resonance imaging and staff discover a forgotten surgical clip in his history. What is the essential pre-scan safety step?
options: Proceed with the scan on a low field strength setting only
Let the patient enter the room first and watch for attraction
Verify the ferromagnetic status of all implanted devices and metallic objects through implant documentation or card checks before entering the scan room
Apply a cold compress to the old surgical site before scanning
items.explanation: MRI zones are controlled by strict screening for ferromagnetic implants and objects, because strong magnetic fields can move implants or metal within the body and cause fatal injury. Safety depends on documented verification of implant type and MRI compatibility before the patient approaches the magnet.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: During a fire in the resuscitation area of the emergency department, what is the correct immediate sequence of actions?
options: Continue resuscitation because the patient is the priority over fire
Call facilities management before doing anything else
Open all doors and windows to ventilate the smoke
Remove all patients from the room immediately, raise the alarm, and use a fire extinguisher if trained and it is safe to do so
items.explanation: Fire response follows the RACE sequence: rescue or remove people from danger, alarm and call the emergency number, contain by closing doors, and extinguish or evacuate as appropriate. Patients must be moved to safety first; continuing procedures, delaying the alarm, or opening doors and fanning flames worsen the emergency.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A community nurse visits a child whose home has exposed electrical wiring, unsecured medications on a low table, and a large unguarded dog. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Document the hazards, remove or secure what is immediately possible, educate the family, and escalate through the appropriate child protection and social services pathway
Ignore the hazards because they are cultural matters
Remove the child from the home immediately without any assessment or discussion
Write a note in the file and take no other action until the next scheduled visit
items.explanation: The nurse should act on identifiable risks by documenting them, reducing immediate danger, counselling the family, and using formal safeguarding referral pathways when children are at risk. Doing nothing breaches duty of care, while removing a child without assessment or due process is disproportionate unless there is imminent serious danger.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Patient Safety and Procedures

items.stem: A competent adult patient with capacity refuses a blood transfusion that his physicians believe is necessary to save his life, on religious grounds. What is the correct legal and ethical position?
options: The transfusion should be given because the doctors know what is best for the patient
The patient's competent refusal must be respected, with efforts to explore his wishes and involve ethics support
The patient's family can overrule him if they agree to the transfusion
Capacity should be declared absent automatically whenever a refusal is made
items.explanation: A competent adult has the right to refuse treatment, even life-saving treatment, and that refusal must be honoured after the decision-making capacity and voluntariness of the choice are confirmed. Substituting medical judgment, family override, or manufactured incapacity are all unlawful and unethical.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A nurse learns from a friend at a social gathering that a famous patient is being treated for a sensitive condition in her ward. What is the appropriate professional response?
options: Confirm the admission to her close friends because they already guessed
Post a general well-wishing message on social media without naming the patient
Refuse to confirm or deny any information and avoid discussing the patient in any setting
Share the information with other colleagues who are not involved in the patient's care
items.explanation: Patient confidentiality extends beyond the clinical setting. Even confirming that someone is a patient can breach privacy, so staff must neither confirm nor deny information and must never discuss identifiable details on social media or with uninvolved colleagues.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A physician realizes he has made a surgical error that has caused additional harm to a patient. What does ethical professional practice require?
options: Conceal the error to protect the reputation of the hospital
Wait to see if the patient develops symptoms before deciding
Blame the scrub nurse publicly in the patient's presence
Disclose the error honestly to the patient or authorized representative, apologize, report through incident systems, and arrange appropriate care
items.explanation: Open disclosure of adverse events, including sincere apology, transparent explanation, incident reporting, and provision of ongoing care, is an ethical and increasingly legal duty. Concealment, delay, and blame-shifting violate trust, professional codes, and the duty of candour.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A dying patient asks her nurse not to tell her family how advanced her illness is, saying she wants to protect them. What should the nurse do?
options: Respect the patient's wishes while exploring her reasons, documenting the discussion, and encouraging her to reconsider sharing information
Tell the family everything immediately because family always has a right to know
Ignore the request and discuss the prognosis with the family at the next ward round
Resign from caring for the patient to avoid the conflict
items.explanation: The duty of confidentiality and respect for autonomy means the competent patient controls disclosure, while staff should sensitively explore her wishes, support her in shared decision-making if possible, and document everything. Families have no automatic right to override a capable patient, and abandoning care is not a solution.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A colleague arrives for a night shift smelling strongly of alcohol and appears unsteady. What is the correct action for the observing nurse?
options: Ignore it because confronting colleagues is not the nurse's role
Inform the nurse in charge or appropriate manager immediately so the colleague is removed from patient-care duties and the issue is managed safely
Cover for the colleague by doing her assignments quietly
Post about the incident on a private social media group for nurses
items.explanation: Fitness-for-duty impairment endangers patients, and staff have a duty to escalate promptly to the responsible manager so the colleague is stood down and supported through the appropriate process. Concealment, informal cover-ups, and public shaming on social media all breach patient safety and professional standards.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A researcher wants to include patients in a clinical trial who are sedated in intensive care. What consent arrangement is ethically acceptable?
options: Take no consent because intensive care patients cannot refuse
Ask any available nurse on the ward to sign as a witness-patient proxy
Seek consent from a legally authorized representative when the patient lacks capacity, with the patient's assent where possible and ethics committee approval in place
Obtain consent from the patient's employer if the patient has no family
items.explanation: Research involving adults lacking capacity requires approval from a research ethics committee and consent from a legally authorized representative, seeking the patient's assent and respecting dissent. Skipping consent, using unqualified proxies, or involving employers breaches research ethics and law.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A patient offers a expensive gift to her surgeon after a successful operation and insists he accept it. What is the most appropriate professional response?
options: Accept the gift privately so that no one else is offended
Accept and then raffle the gift among the ward staff
Accept only if the patient writes a testimonial for the hospital website
Decline graciously in line with professional boundaries and organizational policy, explaining that excellent care is the expected standard
items.explanation: Gifts that are lavish or could influence, or be seen to influence, clinical judgment threaten professional boundaries and public trust. The polite response is to decline in line with policy while acknowledging the patient's gratitude, and to escalate to ethics or management if a gift is persisted with.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A 17-year-old with capacity asks that her parents not be told she is starting contraception. What is the correct approach under typical consent and confidentiality frameworks?
options: Assess and respect her capacity to consent, provide confidential care within the law, and encourage her to involve a trusted adult where safe
Inform the parents regardless of the girl's wishes because she is a minor
Refuse all treatment until a parent attends the clinic
Prescribe contraception and inform the parents afterwards without telling the patient
items.explanation: Many jurisdictions allow mature minors to consent to and receive confidential sexual health care when they have capacity and the treatment is in their interests. Blanket disclosure or blanket refusal ignores both the law and the welfare of the young person, while covert disclosure breaches confidentiality.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: During a ward discussion about a complex case, a student nurse asks questions that lead to the patient's identity and unusual history being discussed in a corridor where visitors pass. What should the team do?
options: Continue the discussion because the corridor is within the hospital
Move the discussion to a private area and reinforce to the student how identifiable information must be protected
Tell the student never to ask questions again
Post the case summary on the staff intranet for further discussion
items.explanation: Clinical discussions about identifiable patients must take place in private settings, not corridors or public areas, because anyone within earshot could overhear confidential information. The teaching moment should reinforce privacy rules rather than silencing the learner or moving the discussion online.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A nurse manager is asked by a journalist to comment on a patient who was injured in a high-profile road traffic accident. What is the correct response?
options: Give general safety advice while confirming the patient's ward to show transparency
Share the information if the journalist promises not to name the hospital
Politely decline to confirm or release any patient information and refer the enquiry to the authorized hospital spokesperson
Ask the patient's employer for permission to comment
items.explanation: Patient information, including the fact of admission, cannot be disclosed to media without proper authorization. Staff should refer all enquiries to the designated spokesperson and never confirm identity or location informally, even with a promise of anonymity.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A physician is asked by a patient's employer for a detailed medical report without the patient's written authorization. What is the legal position?
options: The report must be provided because the employer pays the insurance
Only verbal permission from a family member is required
Anonymized details may be shared freely without consent
The report cannot be disclosed without the patient's valid, specific written consent or another lawful basis
items.explanation: Medical records and reports are confidential and may only be released with the patient's informed, specific written consent or where a clear legal provision applies. Insurance or employment relationships do not by themselves create a right of access, and family verbal permission is insufficient.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A nurse is caring for a patient whose stated religious beliefs require refusal of blood products, and the patient develops a life-threatening anaemia. What is the nurse's ethical duty while supporting the refusal?
options: Respect the refusal while ensuring the patient receives all other acceptable treatments, symptom relief, and clear information about the risks
Transfuse anyway and accept the disciplinary consequences
Leave the ward so as not to be involved
Persuade the patient's children to overrule the refusal
items.explanation: Respecting a capacitated patient's refusal does not mean abandoning them; the team must offer every acceptable alternative therapy, palliate symptoms, and ensure the refusal is informed and revisited if circumstances change. Unilateral transfusion, withdrawal of care, or family coercion all violate professional ethics.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A newly registered nurse discovers that a senior colleague has been charting analgesics that were never given to patients. What should she do?
options: Do nothing because it is not her responsibility as the newest staff member
Raise the concern with the nurse in charge or through the organization's confidential reporting pathway, documenting facts accurately
Confront the colleague publicly on the ward in front of patients
Alter the records to match what she believes really happened
items.explanation: Falsifying medication records is serious professional misconduct and a patient safety risk, and all staff have a duty to report concerns through proper channels with accurate documentation. Staying silent, public confrontation, or tampering with records compound the original wrongdoing.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A patient with end-stage dementia can no longer swallow, and family members disagree about whether to start artificial nutrition and hydration. What is the most appropriate approach?
options: Always continue nutrition and hydration because withholding them is unethical in every case
Follow whichever family member shouts loudest
Explore any valid advance directive, involve the substituted judgment of the legal surrogate, consult the multidisciplinary team and ethics committee, and decide in the patient's best interests
Stop all care immediately because the patient cannot consent
items.explanation: Decisions for patients lacking capacity must be guided by any valid advance directive, then the best interests or substituted judgment standard, with family mediation and ethics committee input when views conflict. Neither automatic continuation nor abrupt withdrawal of all care respects the patient-centered ethical framework.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law

items.stem: A nurse is asked by a patient to help her arrange medically assisted dying, which is illegal in the jurisdiction. What is the correct professional response?
options: Assist the patient because autonomy is the only ethical principle that matters
Report the patient to the police for asking the question
Refer her to a colleague without any explanation
Clearly explain that assistance cannot be provided, listen empathetically to her concerns, and offer access to palliative care and psychological support
items.explanation: Professionals must not participate in unlawful acts, but they also owe duties of compassion and communication. The correct approach is to explain the legal position honestly, explore the suffering driving the request, and connect the patient with palliative care, counselling, and spiritual support rather than punitive or dismissive responses.
items.reference: DOH Abu Dhabi Examination Syllabus - Professional Ethics and Law
